summary: Camille Bulcke was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at KU Leuven (~1927–1930), the University of Calcutta (1942–1944), and the University of Allahabad (1945–1949). He served as Head of the Sanskrit and Hindi Department at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1949–1957).

Camillo Alessio Formigatti specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Milan and completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg (2011) under Harunaga Isaacson and Jürgen Hanneder. He has held posts at Cambridge, Oxford, Hamburg, and the Bodleian Library.

Canan Yoğurt is an Indologist who studied at Ankara University (2006–2010, 2012–2015) and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (2010–2011). She held posts at Erciyes University (2014–2024), the University of Hyderabad (2017), and Çukurova University (2024).

Carel Gabriel Cobet was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He attended Gymnasium Haganum and studied at Leiden University (~1831–1836), where he later held faculty appointments in 1846 and from 1849 to 1884.
Carl A. P. Ruck is a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He was educated at Harvard University and the University of Michigan, and he held a post at Boston University around 1970.

Carl Arendt worked in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1856–1859) under Franz Bopp and Heymann Steinthal. From 1887 to 1902, he was a teacher at the Seminar for Oriental Languages.

Carl Bezold was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied under Friedrich Delitzsch (~1881–1883), founded the Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und Vorderasiatische Archäologie in 1886, and held a post at Heidelberg University from ~1894 to 1922.

Carl Bielefeldt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki, Seizan Yanagida, and at UC Berkeley (~1974–1980). He held long-term posts at Stanford University (~1980–2013) and was associated with the Numata Center.

Carl Brockelmann worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Rostock, Breslau, and Strasbourg under Theodor Nöldeke. He held posts at Breslau, Humboldt University, Königsberg (1903–1910), Halle-Wittenberg (1910–1922), and Frederick William University Berlin (1922–1923).

Carl Cappeller was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Humboldt University under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, Königsberg, Leipzig, and Jena. He served as professor at the University of Jena from 1875 to 1921.
Carl Christian Rafn was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from ~1814 to 1816 and subsequently held a post there.

Carl Darling Buck was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Yale, in Athens, and at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann, August Leskien, and William Dwight Whitney. He was Assistant Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative IE Philology at Chicago (1892–1933).

Carl Ferdinand Friedrich Lehmann-Haupt was a scholar of history and archaeology. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1893–1910), the University of Greifswald (~1911–1914), Istanbul University (~1915–1918), and the University of Innsbruck (~1918–1932).

Carl Fredrik Bergstedt was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Uppsala University (1836–1842) under Otto Fredrik Tullberg, and subsequently studied under Christian Lassen (~1845–1846), Eugène Burnouf (~1846–1847), and Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1846–1848).

Carl Friedrich Gauss studied at TU Braunschweig, the University of Göttingen (under Georg Christoph Lichtenberg and Christian Gottlob Heyne), and Helmstedt. From 1807 to 1855, he served as full professor at Göttingen and director of the Göttingen Observatory.

Carl Friedrich Lottner was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1851–1854) under Franz Bopp. He later held posts at Trinity College, Hartford, as Lecturer in 1860 and Professor of Sanskrit in 1864.

Carl Gaedicke was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Jena, earning his Ph.D. in 1877 under Berthold Delbrück, and also studied under Eduard Sievers and Carl Cappeller.

Carl Gustav Jung studied at the University of Basel (1895–1900). He held posts at the University of Zurich (~1905–1914), ETH Zurich as professor (1933–1942), and the University of Basel as chair of medical psychology (1944).

Carl Gustav Ruben Diehl was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned three degrees at Lund University between 1925 and 1956. He served as Docent at Lund University (1954–1959) and at Uppsala University (1960–1966).

Carl Hjalmar Borgstrøm was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Oslo (1928–1936). He held posts at Trinity College Dublin (1932–1935), Ankara University (1936–1937), Lund University (1945), and the University of Oslo (1947–1976).
